label: ladder rung 10: 2x depth reach at 1s/turn, network only (3.7M knps, DeepLMP, TT-quiesce, zero-alloc SEE) + games opening book, 4 threads
elo_note: Calibrated with 8 threads and 1000 ms time budget. Depth reach at 1s doubled from depth 6-8 to depth 12-13 through direct 1D array ray stepping, zero-alloc SEE, single-probe TT, DeepLMP, quiescence TT probing/storing, and deferred move generation. Hand evaluation dropped 2026-09-16: blending it at 0.45 cost 18% of nodes per second (611-639 knps against 719-749 paired) and +33 +/- 22 Elo over 1000 games at 10 ms a move, SPRT settled better. A 0.20 blend read -18 +/- 24, which is the same finding: at any positive weight the full PositionScoreEval still runs, so only dropping it outright buys the time back. The improving flag was adopted the same day: late move pruning had taken its improving argument as a hardwired false since it was written, and the real two-ply static trend read +12 +/- 15 twice independently, +12 +/- 11 pooled over 4000 games at 10 ms. The network was retrained on 2026-09-18 on a deduplicated corpus: the five pools merged to 10,957,828 distinct positions, 4,797,515 exact duplicates dropped out of 15,755,343 read. It read +15 +/- 11 over 3,600 games at 100 ms, SPRT[0,10] settled better at llr +3.78. The same five pools with their duplicates kept read -19 +/- 20 and self-play positions alone -26 +/- 20, so the gain is the deduplication, not the extra rows. Razoring was adopted 2026-09-18: depths 1 to 3 whose static evaluation stands more than 2.0 + 1.5*depth pawns below the window are verified with a quiescence search instead of searched at full width, which is 94.7% of the plain node count over six positions at depth 7 and +14 +/- 12 over 3,000 games at 100 ms, SPRT[0,10] settled better at llr +3.26.
